title: Share links and viewer-only guest tokens
goal: Viewer-only share links: hosts create and revoke short-lived links, and anonymous visitors exchange a link token for a limited guest relay ticket, with strong abuse controls and no write capability.
scope_in: POST /v1/sessions/{id}/share-links (host, sessions:host, Idempotency-Key accepted): create link with expiry <= 24 h (default 1 h) and max uses (default 10, max 50).
DELETE /v1/sessions/{id}/share-links/{token}: revoke; new joins fail immediately and guests already joined with that link are removed (closed with 4403 via relay notifier).
POST /v1/share-links/{token}/join (public, rate-limited): validate token, create an ephemeral guest member (role viewer) and mint a 60 s single-use relay ticket with role `viewer`.
Token handling: 160-bit URL-safe random token, only sha256 stored, constant-time lookup by hash, never logged.
Entitlement check (relay_access, max_session_members) and session-state check (live or paused only).
Guest records and audit events for create, revoke and each join.
scope_out: Session lifecycle and the other session routes: B053/B054.
Key distribution to guests: the E2E key travels in the URL fragment built by the client; the server never sees or stores it (CT-DEEPLINK, CT-CRYPTO).
Rate-limit middleware internals: B023 (this lane configures buckets).
Workspace invites for named people: B029.
build_against: Fastify inject with fake SessionService (B053/B054 interface), fake ticket signer (Ed25519 test key), in-memory rate limiter from B009, entitlement fixtures. Relay notifier recorded by a fake.
interfaces: POST /v1/sessions/{id}/share-links {expires_in_s?: 60..86400, max_uses?: 1..50} -> 201 {token, url:'https://centcom.dev/j/<token>', expires_at, max_uses}  (token returned once)
POST /v1/share-links/{token}/join {name?: string 1..40} -> 200 {ticket, region, member:{id, slot, role:'viewer'}, session:{id}} ; errors 404 (unknown/expired/revoked, uniform), 429
Tables share_link(id, session_id, token_hash bytea unique, expires_at, max_uses, uses, revoked_at, created_by_member), guest_member(member_id pk 'mem_…', session_id, share_link_id, name, created_at)
acceptance: create by a non-host (editor) returns 403; by the host returns 201 with a token of 43 chars base64url (>=160 bits), expires_at <= now+24 h; expires_in_s=86401 returns 422.
The database row holds sha256(token) only; a dump grep for the plain token finds nothing, and the token does not appear in captured logs.

join with a valid token returns a ticket with claims role='viewer', aud='centcom-relay', exp-iat=60 s and a fresh jti; the guest can never obtain role editor or host (property test over random inputs).

join with an unknown, expired, revoked or exhausted (uses == max_uses) token returns the same 404 problem body and similar latency (timing difference < 5 ms median in test) so tokens cannot be probed.
Concurrent 50 joins on a link with max_uses=10 succeed exactly 10 times (atomic increment), the rest get 404.
revoke makes the next join fail and notifies the relay to close existing guests of that link with 4403 within the same request; revoke by a non-host is 403.
join is refused (409/404) when the session is ended/expired, when relay_access is false for the workspace, or when max_session_members would be exceeded (guests count as members).
11th join attempt from one IP within a minute returns 429 with Retry-After; guest `name` containing control characters is rejected 422.
Guest tickets do not include a `dev` claim and cannot be used to call any REST API (the ticket audience is relay only).
tests: share-links.create-revoke.test.ts: authz, expiry bounds, revocation effects
share-links.join.test.ts: ticket claims, single-use, role invariants
share-links.limits.test.ts: entitlements, member cap, rate limits
share-links.privacy.test.ts: token never stored or logged in plain
guardrails: MUST issue only role 'viewer' tickets for guests; any write-capable role from a share link is a critical defect.
MUST store and compare token hashes only; MUST use constant-time comparison and uniform error responses.
MUST NOT accept or store the E2E key fragment; the join endpoint ignores/rejects any `k` field.
MUST cap link lifetime at 24 h server-side regardless of client input (CT-DEEPLINK).
MUST honour policy.share_history=false by telling the relay the guest may not receive earlier epochs (flag carried as session policy, not as a new claim).
Guest members MUST be deleted when their link expires or the session ends.
failure_modes: Relay notifier down on revoke -> revoke committed; closing of live guests retried via outbox, relay re-checks revoked guests at the next privileged frame (<= 2 s cache).
Ticket signer unavailable -> 503 with retry_after_s and no use consumed (increment rolled back).
Redis rate-limit store unavailable -> fail closed for the public join endpoint (503), open for authenticated create.
